turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come, sit. I will just check the pressure before the doctor calls you. Were you waiting long?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah not so long only. The auto got stuck near the signal, some procession or what, but I reached.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Good. Arm straight please, don't talk for a second.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): This cuff is always tight no? Last time also they told me some number and I forgot it completely.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Today it is 118 over 76, and the pulse is 82. Quite alright. My own sister, she has the thyroid, she panics if the machine even beeps, I keep telling her it is nothing.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, sisters. My own sister is allergic to dust, she cannot even sweep, she starts sneezing like anything.
[SEG0007] person_1 (NURSE): Hmm. Doctor will see you now, you can go in.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hello, I am Dr. Mehta. Tell me, what brings you today?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, this sneezing is killing me. Every spring same story, nose running, eyes itching. I thought it will settle but this year it is worse only.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sneezing, runny nose, itchy eyes. This season, since when?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, started maybe two weeks back, when those yellow trees flowered on our lane. But actually it is every spring, from the last four years or so.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): And in winter, in the monsoon, are you fine, or is the nose running then also?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Ya ya, completely fine. December I even danced at my cousin's wedding, no sneezing. The food was too oily though, ha, whole another topic.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. The itching, both eyes or one?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Both eyes, and they water also. Not pain exactly, just that itchy feeling, I keep rubbing and my husband scolds me.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any wheeze? Whistling sound, or tightness in the chest?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Wheeze? No no, nothing like that. Chest is okay, I climb the stairs to the office fine.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Cough? Any fever?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough, no fever. Only the nose and the eyes. Evening I feel a bit dragged out but that is deadlines only, not illness.

[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hmm. So nose and eyes, not the lung. Let me not jump. It could be spring pollen, it could be house dust, it could be a viral cold, but a cold does not return every April for four years, so I am not calling this an infection today.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): My neighbour said sinus, take antibiotic. I did not take all that. I only take that cetrizine tablet sometimes.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Cetrizine, you mean cetirizine. What strength, and how often is sometimes?

[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): The 10 mg one, small white tablet. When sneezing is too much, maybe two three days in a week, not daily. My sister's doctor gave her some other tablet for the dust, I never asked the name.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay. And when you take it, does it help?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Ya, sneezing comes down. The eyes, not so much, they keep itching even after the tablet.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me look. The lining inside the nose is pale and a bit swollen, watery, both sides. Eyes are pink at the inner corners, no sticky yellow stuff.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that bad? Some WhatsApp forward said pink eye means infection, I got properly scared.

[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): This is not that picture. The pollen sets off the mast cells in the lining, they release histamine, the tiny vessels leak, and that is your watery nose and the itch. The voice box and the lung are not involved, which is why you have no wheeze.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): So the body is fighting the pollen and making a mess. Same as my sister then, she is allergic to dust, I told the nurse outside.

[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Runs in families sometimes, yes. I would not say you have her dust allergy though. Your timing is the spring. I am taking this as seasonal allergic rhinitis, a working impression, not something a lab has proved.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): So no blood test? I skipped breakfast in case, now I am hungry only.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): No blood test, no scan. We see how a proper daily antihistamine treats you. I will not conclude asthma, and I will not conclude sinusitis, not from today's story.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Good, I hate those machines. My colleague did a CT last month for headache, such a drama, and it was just stress.

[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): We will stop the on-and-off cetirizine. I want fexofenadine 120 mg, one tablet every morning, right through this season. And olopatadine eye drops, one drop in each eye, morning and night.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Fexofenadine, 120, morning. Drops twice. Err, will the drops burn?
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): More a cool feeling than a burn. If you use contact lenses, take them out, put the drop, wait fifteen minutes. Do you use lenses?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): No, only spectacles for reading. And the cetirizine, I should throw the strip?

[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Don't throw it, just don't take it on the same days as the new tablet. One antihistamine, not two. If the eyes are still miserable after two weeks we can rethink the drops, but we are starting them now, not waiting.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. Next weekend I am going to my mother's place in Jaipur, the trees there are worse I think, whole garden.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Take the morning tablet even on the travel days. Keep the car windows up if you can. Come and see me in four weeks, Jaipur or no Jaipur.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Four weeks, noted. Should I bring my sister along, she keeps asking me to ask you.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): She needs her own visit, I can't treat her off your account. For you, any throat pain, any ear block?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): No, throat is fine, ears are fine. Only this nose and eye business.
[SEG0044] person_1 (NURSE): Sorry, just a second. Next patient is already inside the corridor. And doctor, my child has football after school so I am leaving sharp at four, I have told the desk.
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fine. So for you, fexofenadine every morning, olopatadine drops twice a day, cetirizine stopped, and review in four weeks. Prescription you can collect outside.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you doctor. This time I will take it properly, not sometimes-sometimes.

spec.situation: Sneezing, itchy eyes and runny nose every spring; takes cetirizine 'sometimes'; sister is allergic to dust; no wheeze; doctor changes antihistamine and adds eye drops.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

features: doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

omissions.text: Eyes itch persists despite cetirizine, although sneezing improves with it.
No blood test and no scan are planned.
Doctor stated he would not conclude asthma and would not conclude sinusitis based on today's story.
Watery nasal discharge was noted on exam ('watery, both sides').
Patient does not use contact lenses; only spectacles for reading.
